meta.title: Auto Session Title
meta.description: Model-generated session titles that follow the latest task, keep your manual renames, persist their settings, and never fail silently.

en.builtinDisabled: Disabled (the slot belongs to this plugin)
en.builtinUntouched: Not taken over (the Host entry is untouched)
en.cadenceFirst: Only the first prompt of a session
en.cadenceHint: Takes effect immediately, no restart needed.
en.conflict: The settings changed elsewhere; the latest values were reloaded, please retry.
en.failureHint: Paste this text back to get it diagnosed.
en.failureSuperseded: This failure was superseded by a successful generation at {at}; it is not a current fault.
en.intro: Session titles follow the latest task automatically. A title you renamed yourself is never overwritten.
en.manualPinned: This title was renamed by hand and will not be overwritten.
en.modelHint: Leave both blank to follow the session model (then the host default chat model). To pin one, fill in both fields — never just one.
en.promptHint: This replaces the built-in instruction; the output contract is always kept. Leave blank to restore the built-in instruction.
en.promptPlaceholder: Leave blank for the built-in instruction
en.sessionsHint: "Regenerate" recomputes one session title right away and hands you either the new title or the raw error.
en.skippedValue: {count} (sub-session labels, manual renames, or nothing to cite)
en.typeSchemeApplyNow: Saving switches to these words right away.
en.typeSchemeBuiltinReadonly: A built-in scheme cannot be edited. To change one, press “New (copy current)” and edit the copy.
en.typeSchemeChooseHint: Switching only affects the next title; titles already written are never rewritten.
en.typeSchemeDeleteConfirm: Deleting removes these words from this machine; if they are in use, the page falls back to the default 22-word scheme. Continue?
en.typeSchemeIntro: The second field answers what this session is doing. Which words it may use is yours to decide: the built-in 10-word scheme is engineering-shaped, the 22-word scheme (the default) spreads across domains, and you can write your own.
en.typeSchemeLimit: {min}–{max} words each, up to {schemes} custom schemes.
en.typeSchemeRefusedConflict: another window changed the settings; they were read again
en.typeSchemeRefusedDomainConflict: a word collides with a domain name or alias
en.typeSchemeRefusedDuplicateName: a scheme already carries that name
en.typeSchemeRefusedDuplicateWord: a word repeats, or two words share a spelling
en.typeSchemeRefusedInvalidName: the name is unusable (empty, or carrying a space, `, * or _)
en.typeSchemeRefusedInvalidWord: a word is unusable (it must be one word, with no spaces)
en.typeSchemeRefusedReservedName: the name collides with a built-in scheme
en.typeSchemeRefusedReservedScheme: a built-in scheme cannot be deleted
en.typeSchemeRefusedStorage: the write failed, so nothing was saved
en.typeSchemeRefusedWordCount: the number of words is outside the range
en.typeSchemeRows: Type words (one per line: word | 中文 | criteria)
en.typeSchemeRowsHint: The word is what the model writes into the title: a single word, no spaces, and it also appears verbatim in an English title. 中文 is what a Chinese title prints. The criteria line is what the model reads; it may be left empty.
en.vocabularyAliasLimitHint: How many other spellings one domain may remember — default {default}, with no ceiling. They never reach the prompt; they only let a domain recognise itself under another name. 0 stops recording new ones.
en.vocabularyAliasPlaceholder: another spelling the model may write
en.vocabularyAliasTrimmed: {stored} spellings are stored but the limit is {limit}, so only the first {limit} are in force.
en.vocabularyCandidateBlocked: Seen in {sessions} sessions, so it has earned a domain of its own — but the domain limit is full at {limit}: raise the limit, or remove a domain.
en.vocabularyCandidatesEmpty: No candidates, so every object word the model wrote matches an existing domain.
en.vocabularyConflictsEmpty: No conflicts: every spelling belongs to exactly one domain.
en.vocabularyConflictsIntro: When two or more domains claim the same spelling, containment matching drops it for all of them — none of these domains can recognise it. Change one of the spellings, or accept that it takes no part in matching.
en.vocabularyDomainLimitHint: How many domains may be offered to the model at once — default {default}, with no ceiling. A longer list makes the model likelier to pick the wrong domain; lowering it makes a new domain harder to earn a slot; 0 stops listing any domain at all.
en.vocabularyDroppedDomains: The domain limit is {limit}, so these {count} domains are not offered to the model (their words stay in the parser table, the model just cannot see them): {list}
en.vocabularyEditHint: Saving replaces every spelling this machine keeps for the domain; the ones the plugin ships are untouched.
en.vocabularyEnvLocalOnly: These names are read on this machine only and never leave it.
en.vocabularyHiddenNotice: This page hides {count} candidates; the Host still keeps them. Reload the page to show them again.
en.vocabularyHideTitle: This only hides the candidate on this page; the Host keeps it.
en.vocabularyIntro: The first title field is a domain name: the plugin starts from a fixed set that matches the conversation, grows new domains from your own sessions, and never invents one silently.
en.vocabularyLabelField: Domain name (printed in the title’s first field)
en.vocabularyLabelFixed: A domain the plugin ships: the plugin names it, so only its spellings can change here.
en.vocabularyLearnAuto: Grow automatically: domains detected in the environment are switched on; one topical word seen in 2 or more sessions becomes a new domain; a longer spelling the model wrote is added as another alias of that domain.
en.vocabularyLearnConfirm: Nominate only: candidates wait below for you; nothing is switched on automatically.
en.vocabularyLearnOff: Off: no learning, no probing, only the built-in domains.
en.vocabularyLimits: domain limit {domains} (adjustable, no ceiling) / {aliases} spellings per domain (adjustable, no ceiling) / {candidates} candidates kept
en.vocabularyLimitsLegacy: up to {domains} domains / {aliases} aliases each / {candidates} candidates kept
en.vocabularyNewFull: The domain limit is reached: remove one, or raise the limit.
en.vocabularyNewHint: The domain appears below at once, and can be renamed or removed like any other.
en.vocabularyPickDomain: Pick the domain to merge into
en.vocabularyRefusedAlias: a spelling is not usable (one word, no punctuation or separator)
en.vocabularyRefusedAliasConflict: that spelling already belongs to another domain
en.vocabularyRefusedConflict: the settings changed elsewhere (learning, or another window); read them again and save
en.vocabularyRefusedDomainLimit: the domain limit is reached: remove one, or raise the limit
en.vocabularyRefusedFixed: the plugin names this domain, so only its spellings can change
en.vocabularyRefusedLabel: the domain name is not usable (one word, no punctuation or separator)
en.vocabularyRefusedLabelConflict: another domain already answers to that name, and the title would print it
en.vocabularyRefusedLimit: the spelling limit is reached: drop one, or raise the limit
en.vocabularyRefusedScope: the guidance line is not usable (it cannot be empty or too long)
en.vocabularyRefusedStorage: the write failed, so nothing was saved
en.vocabularyResetConfirm: Resetting drops every domain, alias and candidate added on this machine; built-in domains are untouched. Continue?
en.vocabularyScopeField: Guidance (one line sent to the model with every title)
en.vocabularySpellingsEmpty: none (saving drops every spelling this machine kept for it)
